topic.instructions:
What is the topic of `article`?

Identify the main claim the article develops: what happened, changed, or is being explained. Select the category that describes this claim, considering the supplied headline and article text together.

Distinguish the subject of the main claim from its participants, setting, communication medium, and supporting evidence. Any of these may itself be the subject; otherwise its mere presence does not determine the category.

Use business when the main claim concerns economic activity, financial outcomes, or the commercial organization and economic performance of an enterprise. Determine the category from the economic substance of the claim, regardless of the industry involved.

Use sci_tech when the main claim concerns a technology’s capabilities, how it works, or how it is developed. Its application belongs here when the article explains the technical capability being provided.

Use sci_tech when the central claim presents scientific knowledge, a research finding, or an explanation of how a phenomenon works. Determine whether the text develops an investigation or explanation; the presence of measurements or numerical data alone does not establish a scientific focus.

Use world when the main claim concerns the exercise of public authority, collective political action, or relations between societies and states. Determine whether the article develops the public process itself or its consequences for another field.

Use sports when the central claim concerns sporting activity: its preparation, competitive performance, results, or organization. Determine the category from the activity being discussed.

Use world when the central claim concerns public or cultural life, or an event and its consequences for people and communities. Distinguish this focus from an investigation of mechanisms, economic activity, or technical capabilities by identifying what the text actually explains.

When several subjects are developed, compare how directly each accounts for the article’s substantive claims and supporting detail. Select the category with the strongest support in the supplied text. Do not invent missing context or use a fixed ordering of categories to resolve equal support.

topic.instructions:
What is the topic of `article`?

Read the headline and description together. Choose the supplied category that best describes the report's central subject and development.

Treat the categories as broad news topics:
- world: political, civic, social, cultural and international affairs, public safety and community affairs.
- sports: sporting activity, participants in their sporting roles, and the organization and governance of sport.
- business: economic activity, markets, financial performance, commercial strategy, relations and operations.
- sci_tech: scientific activity, discoveries and observations of natural phenomena, and the development, availability, adoption, operation, use and evaluation of technology.

Cover descriptive reports as well as explanatory ones. When topics overlap, consider both the field and what is being reported about it. Determine whether financial, legal or organizational information is the central subject or supporting context; do the same for the identity and industry of the participants. Choose the category that best captures the report's main information. Use only the supplied text and do not apply a fixed ordering of categories.

topic.instructions:

Use the supplied category descriptions as the definitions of the available answers. Preserve their full scope; do not add requirements, exclusions, or a fixed preference between categories.

When more than one category fits, compare the support for each under the supplied descriptions and choose the one that best accounts for the article as a whole. Use only the supplied content; do not invent missing context to resolve ambiguity.
